submitter: bugfix_029_retry_kills_live_child workstream (029 closed; this is its last residual)
rationale:
ROUND 2. Round 1 was REVISE on a HIGH gating objection from editquality, and it was RIGHT: "The plan's own rationale says 'workflow% adds 2' … It does not cover v_active_workflows or v_all_workflows, which are prefixed 'v_', not 'workflow'. Both are named in the same run dd61df1b DataRequests[0].why quote as tables the loop needed and could not describe. The fix is real but only half-covers the cited failure."

The contradiction was inside one document: I justified omitting the views with 'no run has yet stalled on one' while my own grounded_in quoted the run asking for them by name. Round 2 covers all four tables the run needed.

The diagnosis bundle's Schema section is populated by a relevance include applied as `table_name ILIKE $n` — a PREFIX match. The default patterns are site%, page%, content%, flow%. `flow%` therefore does NOT match `workflow%`, and never has. That is almost certainly not what was intended, and it is not free.

It cost a real diagnosis run. Run dd61df1b (the bugs_closed/301 lane, page-build-handler ownership ordering) returned UNVERIFIABLE with a data_request whose stated reason was: 'These tables (found via a prior data_request) are not in the bundle's schema listing … need their columns before a follow-up query can pull page-build-handler's actual step sequence.' The tables were workflow_templates, workflow_contract_chain, v_active_workflows, v_all_workflows. The loop had the right hypothesis and the right target and could not write the query.

This is the same class as commit 0132a3683 (council-approved round 1, corr e03f7122), which added awaited_requests to schemaAlwaysTables after TWO 090 runs on bugs_open/029 died the same way, and the same class as run 074beb8a before that. Three separate lanes, four wasted runs, one cause: a table the bundle cannot describe. That fix deliberately did not widen the include, because the include gap is a different lane's symptom and deserved its own rationale. This is that rationale.

The change is one pattern in a list. It ships no new mechanism, no new key, no new authority, and no new capability — it makes an existing, already-reviewed filter cover two more tables.

plan.summary: Add "workflow%" AND "v%workflow%" to defaultSchemaInclude, so the bundle describes all FOUR tables run dd61df1b needed: workflow_templates, workflow_contract_chain, v_active_workflows, v_all_workflows. Document the prefix semantics and the measured sizing, and test both patterns plus the fact that workflow% cannot reach the v_-prefixed views.

edits.rationale: Two patterns. Sizing measured: the full predicate resolves to 33 of 479 public tables today — matching a live bundle's own header line verbatim — and goes to 35 with workflow% and 37 with v%workflow%, against a schema_table_cap of 120. "v%workflow%" rather than "v_%" deliberately: the latter is a net for a naming convention and pulls in 11 unrelated views, whereas this is scoped to the domain and resolves to exactly the two the run named. ("_" is also a single-character wildcard in LIKE, so "v_%" is broader than it looks.)

The entry's REASON is invisible from the code — someone assuming flow% already covers workflow tables would tidy it back out. First assertion guards the entry; second asserts the PREFIX semantics that make it necessary, so if matching ever becomes a contains-match the test says workflow% is now redundant rather than leaving both in place for reasons nobody recalls. Proven able to fail by mutation: removing the pattern fails it with the intended message. Round 2 adds guards for v%workflow% by name and asserts that workflow% does NOT reach the v_-prefixed views — because the omission was argued for once already and a future reader will reach for the same reasoning.
edits.sketch:
if !has("workflow%") { t.Error(`"workflow%" missing — "flow%" does NOT cover workflow_* under a prefix match; run dd61df1b stalled on exactly that`) }
if matchesPrefix("flow%", "workflow_templates") { t.Error("prefix matching has changed: workflow% is now redundant") }

grounded_in: 090 run dd61df1b DataRequests[0].why, 2026-08-19 — "These tables (found via a prior data_request) are not in the bundle's schema listing and agent_definitions' own workflow columns are NULL for page-build-handler; need their columns before a follow-up query can pull page-build-handler's actual step sequence to check the claimed step ordering." The SQL it could not run named workflow_templates, workflow_contract_chain, v_active_workflows, v_all_workflows.
diagnose_load_runtime_action.go, gatherSchema — the include is applied as `table_name ILIKE $n` with no leading wildcard, i.e. a prefix match, which is why flow% has never matched workflow%.

Live DB measured 2026-08-21 — the full selection predicate resolves to 33 of 479 public tables, matching a live bundle's own header ("33 of 479 public tables are shown"); workflow% adds exactly 2; schema_table_cap default is 120.

Prior art, same class: commit 0132a3683 (awaited_requests to schemaAlwaysTables, council-approved round 1, corr e03f7122) after two 090 runs on bugs_open/029 stalled; and the pre-existing in-file record of run 074beb8a, which guessed a column name, got SQLSTATE 42703 and stopped at UNVERIFIABLE for the same reason.
Live agent_definitions query 2026-08-21 — NO active agent config sets schema_include_patterns, so the Go default is what is in force and this change is not shadowed by config.

Live DB measured 2026-08-21, round 2 — "v%workflow%" resolves to exactly v_active_workflows and v_all_workflows (2 tables); "v_%" would add 11 unrelated views. Totals: 33 before, 35 with workflow%, 37 with both, cap 120.
Council round 1 verdict, corr b353d731-6164-4178-8c1f-c483965db790: REVISE, gating objection from editquality, severity high — the quote reproduced verbatim in the rationale above.
